updates.title: Inventory opens on the Active tab, with the Inactive tab beside it
preconditions: Needs: 1 user (Admin) · 1 browser · about 5 minutes
Build: the Part Lifecycle QA build (no build exists yet; use the build named in the test run).

User: [User-A], signed in with the Admin role. Admin holds the 'Part Library & Inventory' permissions View, Create & Edit and Delete by default (Settings → Roles & Permissions); Delete is what allows Deactivate parts and Activate parts.
Location: [Loc-1], any one location [User-A] can pick in the location selector in the top bar.
Browser: a desktop browser window at least 1280 pixels wide (parts management is desktop and tablet only).
Data: 1 active, tracked part of this case at [Loc-1]: [Part-A] (example part number ZZAUTOTEST-PL-TABS-01). The number and description are examples; the part must be active and stocked at [Loc-1].
setup: 1. Sign in as [User-A] and pick [Loc-1] in the location selector in the top bar.

2. Create [Part-A]: go to Parts → Inventory, click New Inventory Part, type Description "ZZAUTOTEST PL tabs part" and Part Number ZZAUTOTEST-PL-TABS-01 (examples), pick any Category (e.g. the first one offered), type Cost (e.g. 10.00) and Sell Price (e.g. 20.00), leave "Track quantities and cost of goods" on, keep the default bin with Quantity 5, and click Save. 3. Check the setup worked: on Parts → Inventory, Active tab, type [Part-A] in the Search box; exactly one row shows [Part-A]. If not, repeat step 2.
steps: 1. In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
2. Look at the area between the page title "Inventory" and the table.
3. Type [Part-A] in the Search box.
4. Click the Inactive tab.
5. Click the Active tab.
results: Step 1: The Inventory page opens with two tabs, "Active" and "Inactive", and "Active" is the selected tab (shown in blue) without you clicking it.

Step 2: The two tabs sit on their own line directly under the title "Inventory". The search and filter row (Search, Bin Location, Category, Supply, the columns icon, the ⋮ menu and New Inventory Part) sits below the tabs, not beside them.
Step 3: The Active tab lists [Part-A] (1 row).
Step 4: "Inactive" becomes the selected tab and [Part-A] is not listed there.
Step 5: "Active" is selected again and [Part-A] is listed again.

updates.title: Parts that existed before the release are active and tracked
preconditions: Needs: 1 user (Admin) · 1 browser · access to the test environment before the Part Lifecycle build is deployed to it (for Setup step 1) · about 15 minutes
Build: the Part Lifecycle QA build (no build exists yet; use the build named in the test run).

User: [User-A], signed in with the Admin role. Admin holds the 'Part Library & Inventory' permissions View, Create & Edit and Delete by default (Settings → Roles & Permissions); Delete is what allows Deactivate parts and Activate parts.
Location: [Loc-1], any one location [User-A] can pick in the location selector in the top bar.
Browser: a desktop browser window at least 1280 pixels wide (parts management is desktop and tablet only).

Data: 3 parts at [Loc-1] that existed before the Part Lifecycle build was deployed and have not been changed since: [Old-1], [Old-2], [Old-3]. [Old-2] has a quantity above 0 and Min and Max set. This case only reads them; it changes nothing.
setup: 1. Before the Part Lifecycle build is deployed, sign in on the earlier build as [User-A], pick [Loc-1], and create 3 parts the way that build allows (Parts → Catalog → New Catalog Part, then Parts → Inventory → New Inventory Part picking that catalog part), with part numbers such as ZZAUTOTEST-PL-RELEASE-01, -02 and -03, Quantity 4 each, and on -02 Min 1 and Max 6.

2. If the build was deployed before step 1 could be done, pick instead any 3 parts that the Inventory list at [Loc-1] showed before the deployment and that nobody has changed since (this case does not change them).
3. [Old-1], [Old-2], [Old-3] = the three part numbers. [Old-2-Min] and [Old-2-Max] = the Min and Max [Old-2] had before the deployment (e.g. 1 and 6).

4. Check the setup worked: on the Part Lifecycle build, Parts → Inventory, the Search box finds each of [Old-1], [Old-2] and [Old-3] on one of the two tabs. If one is not found, replace it with another part that existed before the deployment.
steps: 1. Sign in on the Part Lifecycle build as [User-A].
2. Pick [Loc-1] in the location selector in the top bar.

5. Replace the search text with [Old-2].
6. Replace the search text with [Old-3].
7. Click the Inactive tab.
8. Type [Old-1] in the Search box.
9. Replace the search text with [Old-2].
10. Replace the search text with [Old-3].
